This meta is referenced enough times that it should be either SceneStringName or a constant somewhere.
Note that `callable_mp()` does not support default arguments, so if something calls the callback without the new argument, it won't work anymore.
On another look, I don't think this part is necessary for anything. `set_text_with_selection()` is only called from SpinBox to get rid of prefix/suffix.
`DisplayServerAndroid::_window_callback()` always assumed that callbacks would have only one argument, which is not the case anymore with `input_text_callback` with this PR. Hence the new template.
I left a "fix" here. Technically, we should always create an undo state only if the action was needed, isn't it?

Thanks for the heads up. I changed the Android display server accordingly.

Since you are adding a new method anyway, you could make it handle both emitting and not emitting the signal (it can be a parameter). And the method could be renamed to something that isn't an implementation detail, like `_push_text_input()`.
You mean something like `{Line,Text}Edit::_push_text_input(const String &p_text, bool p_emit_signal)`?
Yes. This way you have only one method that should be called in this case and its use-case is more clear.

I followed @YeldhamDev's suggestion: I created instead a private public API `_set_text()` function that is essentially the implementation of the public `set_text()`.

body: I will test the performance impact, but as I intend to make JavaScript use letter prefixes like the main code base, it is bound to happen again. But yeah, I could put `pEvent` for now in the list and deal with more use-cases later.

It would work! (with making it's something like `set_text_with_text_changed_signal` instead of no signal if emit signal is true). The whole point of the PR is to fix the issue of the Web platform not being able to send individual key text inputs to the engine directly, that making the `text_changed` signal never fire.
But it would change the design of the Window call from duck typing to literally only call `{Line,Text}Edit` instances. If we're ok with this, I'll make the change. Good idea, as I'm not too fond of creating public/private APIs.

Ah I missed that it was already using `call()` before your changes.

Then yeah I'm not sure if this was done because it's simpler than casting, or to support potential other nodes implementing this method.

I suspect it's the former but this should be checked. It might also be to reduce dependencies so Windows doesn't need to include LineEdit/TextEdit (in case it doesn't yet).

Regarding the private API, another option would be to make it actually public, with a name like `set_text_no_signal`. I believe we added a couple methods like this in Control classes in recent releases.

Not sure which option I'd favor tbh.

> Regarding the private API, another option would be to make it actually public, with a name like `set_text_no_signal`. I believe we added a couple methods like this in Control classes in recent releases.

Take note that the signal is already NOT emitted when calling `set_text()` by design. So the new function would be awkwardly `set_text_with_text_changed_signal()` (or just `set_text_and_signal()`). See the note at the end of the property [`LineEdit.text` in the docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_lineedit.html#class-lineedit-property-text).

I would not expose it as public. Since the whole text input API should be probably refactored to unify virtual keyboard with IME (currently using `NOTIFICATION_OS_IME_UPDATE` notification and display server methods).
